input_messages.content: Hi there. I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

I’m at home here in the United States, not traveling anywhere. As for calls, yes, I can make regular phone calls just fine. I’m not sure about the mobile data or browsing the web—I don’t really use the internet much on my phone. Is there a simple way to check that?

I see that my phone shows a good signal and says "5G" at the top, and I think mobile data is enabled. Does that mean my mobile data is working, or do I still need to try opening a website? I just want to make sure I’m doing this right.
Alright, I’ll give that a try. Just to double-check, opening a website won’t mess up anything on my phone or use up a lot of my data, will it? I get a bit nervous with these things.
I tried to check my internet connection, but it looks like there’s no connection at all. Does this mean my mobile data isn’t working? What should I do next?

Oh, I see. I definitely don’t want to change my plan, but I’d be okay with adding more data if that’s what I need to do. Could you please add 2GB for me? And just to be sure, that will be $4.00, right? I just want to make sure I understand before anything is changed.
Yes, please go ahead and add the 2GB for $4.00. I just want to be able to send my picture messages again. Thank you for explaining everything so clearly.

I just tried to send a picture message again, but it still isn’t working. Is there something else I should try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—will I lose anything important if we keep troubleshooting?

I checked, and my phone shows a good signal, “5G,” and something that says “Data Enabled” at the top. Does that mean my mobile data is already turned on, or do I still need to do something else? I’m not sure what kind of phone I have, but I hope this helps.

I found something called “APN Name: internet” and “MMSC URL: http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc” in my phone’s settings. I’m not sure what any of that means. Do I still need to reset anything, or does it look okay to you? I really don’t want to mess anything up.
I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to worry that something’s really wrong with my phone.
I checked, and it looks like Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. What should we try next?

I checked my messaging app, and it looks like it only has permission for “phone.” It doesn’t seem to have access to storage or SMS. Do I need to change something here? I’m not sure how to do that on my own.

I’m not really sure what kind of phone I have, but the app I use is just called “messaging.” The phone isn’t fancy—just a regular one with a screen and some buttons on the side. Does that help? I’d really appreciate step-by-step instructions, but please keep them simple for me.

Alright, I followed your instructions and turned on both “storage” and “SMS” permissions for my messaging app. I just tried sending a picture message, and it finally worked! Thank you so much for your patience and help—I really appreciate it.

Thank you so much for your help and for being so patient with me. I really appreciate it. I’ll let you know if I have any more trouble, but for now, I’m just happy I can send pictures of my grandkids again! Have a great day. ###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

2. Scroll down and find “Apps” or “Applications” and tap on it.
3. Look for your “messaging” app in the list and tap on it.
4. Tap on “Permissions.”
5. You should see a list of permissions like “Storage,” “SMS,” and “Phone.”
6. If “Storage” and “SMS” are not enabled, tap on each one and select “Allow.”

After you’ve enabled both “Storage” and “SMS” permissions, try sending a picture message again.
